name: San Bartolo Yautepec Zapotec, author's abbreviation 'zsby'

catalog_quote: Al igual que otras lenguas zapotecas, el zsby es una lengua tonal. Contrasta tres tonos: alto, bajo y ascendente. [...] Se trata de una lengua predominantemente monosilábica; es decir, que la mayor parte de las raíces verbales y nominales se conforman por una sola sílaba pesada [...]. Además, todos los bisílabos y trisílabos que encontramos en la lengua se pueden analizar como el producto de la composición de dos o más raíces monosilábicas; por alguna sílaba proveniente de la epéntesis vocálica, o como préstamos del español. En todas estas palabras de dos o tres sílabas, el acento siempre recae sobre la última, sin contar los enclíticos que se asocian al lado derecho de las raíces nominales o verbales, los cuales no influyen en la asignación del acento en la palabra fonológica. De hecho, el criterio que permite definir la palabra fonológica como un componente prosódico en el zsby es el acento, pues cada palabra fonológica posee un único acento principal. Los correlatos acústicos del acento implican una mayor duración y una estructura formántica más definida en las vocales respecto de otras vocales adyacentes. [...] La tonía o F0 no es un correlato acústico para el acento en el zsby, ya que estamos ante una lengua tonal y el F0 se emplea principalmente para realizar distinciones tonales.

new_statements.translation: Like other Zapotec languages, SBY Zapotec is a tonal language. It contrasts three tones: high, low and rising. [...] It is a predominantly monosyllabic language [...]. In all these words of two or three syllables, stress always falls on the last one, not counting the enclitics that attach to the right of nominal or verbal roots, which do not influence stress assignment in the phonological word. In fact, the criterion that allows the phonological word to be defined as a prosodic constituent in SBY Zapotec is stress, since each phonological word has a single main stress. The acoustic correlates of stress involve greater duration and a more defined formant structure [...]. Pitch or F0 is not an acoustic correlate of stress in SBY Zapotec.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Tonal language (H, L, rising) with a separate stress accent: roots are mostly monosyllabic; in any polysyllabic word (compounds, words with epenthetic syllables, Spanish loans) the single main stress falls on the final syllable of the root/lexical word; enclitics adjoin to the phonological word after stress assignment and are never stressed. Stress is cued by duration and vowel quality, not F0.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned. The first (unstressed) element of a compound loses laryngealization and changes tone (p. 123).
new_statements.exceptions: None to the final-stress rule; enclitics are explicitly outside the stress domain (p. 123, p. 147: 'que siempre recae en la última sílaba de la raíz'). Historical note p. 128: stress direction changed from trochaic to iambic.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (root + enclitics by adjunction), in a predominantly monosyllabic language; the rule is stated for di- and trisyllabic words. Author's label 'zsby' = zapoteco de San Bartolo Yautepec, ISO zpb, ~110 speakers all over 60 (p. 122).
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes the Zapotec of San Bartolo Yautepec (author's abbreviation zsby; ISO 639-3 zpb = Glottolog yaut1235), the divergent variety also called Dizdea/Dí'zdéh; the author classifies it as Central Zapotec with Sierra Sur areal features (p. 122), Hernández Luna & Herrera 2024 place it in the Miahuatecan branch, and Beam de Azcona 2019 as probable Central Zapotec. Not to be confused with the Cisyautepecan ('Yautepec district') Zapotec varieties (e.g. Quiegolani, San Pedro Mixtepec, Quioquitani quio1241) or Transyautepecan (Quiavicuzas).

sources.note: p. 123: language is tonal (high, low, rising) and predominantly monosyllabic; in all di-/trisyllabic words (compounds, epenthetic syllables, Spanish loans) stress always falls on the last syllable, enclitics excluded; one main stress per phonological word; cues = duration and formant definition, not F0. p. 147: enclitics adjoin without affecting stress, 'que siempre recae en la última sílaba de la raíz'. p. 128: historically trochaic > iambic.
